PC gaming is technically better. These are the pros:

- Higher framerate and better graphics in all games

- you will learn about PC hardware and will be able to replace individual pieces if they break. You can upgrade parts of your PC over the years

- PCs are useful for other things: programming, game development, video/photo-editing, 3-d modelling, office work, browsing, file sharing, cryptocurrency mining... PCs are tools, consoles are toys meant for entertainment

- Games can be modified and improved by hobby game developers (mods, modders, modding), in comparison, consoles are.locked down

- There are DRM-free (no copy-protection) games on PC. Not all games are DRM-free, most big games have some kind of DRM

- PC games are easier to back-up (and pirate)

- PCs have emulators, so you can play games from old consoles

It can be tricky to build a better PC with the same money you could get a console with, especially when consoles are on sale. They sell the console to you at a loss and make it up by selling more expensive games. Games on PC are much cheaper (see isthereanydeal.com).

Despite these overwhelming advantages there is one tradeoff or drawback to PC gaming...

Competitive multiplayer games on PC are more difficult and are played at a higher skill-level than on consoles. You have to play many multiplayer games with mouse and keyboard or you will have no chance at winning. As a result, playing multiplayer on PC more exciting and has more depth, but it is also more stressful. There are also more cheaters in PC games, using cheat software ("hacks") which can ruin the game completely for everyone else, although chats aren't unseen on console, it requires a lot more effort to deploy cheats, requiring a mod-chip etc. I simply find playing with a controller on the couch more comfortable sometimes. I used to play more on PC, but now when I want to play a multiplayer game on me to relax, I play often on console these days.
